title: FR: allow purchasing the Mullvad add-on from more countries
body:
The current region availability list ("countries in which you can purchase the Tailscale Mullvad add-on") is here:
https://tailscale.com/kb/1258/mullvad-exit-nodes/#available-regions

This is a tracking bug to sell the add-on in more countries.

_Discussions about international policy or legal status in this ticket are not useful or fruitful and are better had elsewhere. Upvotes may increase the priority for specific regions, but legal and policy discussions will not._

----

### What are you trying to do?

use Mullvad

### How should we solve this?

Make it available :)

### What is the impact of not solving this?

I can't use Mullvad

comments.author: participant11
comments.body:
Not everything is a conspiracy. We did the Mullvad integration because most operating systems really don't like multiple VPN programs running at the same time, fighting over various system settings. By adding Mullvad support to the Tailscale client, the operating systems see only one program messing with various networking settings (routes, firewall, DNS). If you don't like Tailscale's Mullvad integration, feel free to keep using Mullvad's client directly instead. (But if the two conflict and you run into problems you'll see why we added Mullvad support into Tailscale.)

For various reasons, we can't just open up Mullvad access to the whole world. We would like that (it would make our job easier), but it's not possible. We've had lawyers and others investigate all this and continue to do so.

> tailscale has only credit card and they even ask for full a billing address

Yes, we didn't change our billing system. Credit cards are a pretty standard way to accept money on the internet.

If you'd like to pay in cash by snail mail or Bitcoin, we're not what you're looking for. That's not our goal. You can continue to use Mullvad directly for such use cases.

comments.author: participant41
comments.body:
@participant11 Rather than mock me, how about you answer the serious question.

On your website you claim:

> As with any traffic on your tailnet, Tailscale cannot access any user traffic sent to Mullvad servers. All user traffic is encrypted in WireGuard tunnels, and Tailscale cannot decrypt this information.

Therefore, I ask again. 

If:

1. Tailscale genuinely do not have any visibility over the traffic  AND 
2. Mullvad are genuinely the operators of the server on the other side

What, exactly, is the difference to a lawyer if the traffic is destined to Mullvad in Sweden or Mullvad in Timbuktu ?  The encryption is the same.

Or is there something we are not being told.

This is a genuine question that deserves a genuine answer and not mockery.

Note that Mozilla VPN is also not available in Australia or Japan. Or Norway or Germany or India or Taiwan or Hong Kong or South Korea or Indonesia.

comments.body:
Going by your argument, that would mean you should be blocking use of Tailscale altogether in e.g. Japan.    You can't provide encryption for one thing and not the other.

As others (e.g. @participant40 ) have said, you're happy to bill Tailscale customers in Australia, presumably for providing Tailscale VPN services in Australia ?  But its a big deal that requires lawyers advice to provide access to Mullvad Australia ?  None of this makes sense....

How about just letting people bring their own Mullvad subscription.   Provide a place in the Admin GUI where people can enter a Mullvad account number and then you are not responsible for selling or providing anything.

I was doing a PoC, on the verge of recommending a Tailscale deployment.   But the lack of clarity is on this topic is ringing bells, and raising red flags everywhere.

It might not be smoke and mirrors, but it sure stinks of it.

When you buy Tailscale without Mullvad, you don't get exit nodes. You get encryption between your own devices.

When you buy the Tailscale Mullvad add-on, you're buying exit nodes via Tailscale.

I am not a lawyer, but presumably there's some legal difference.

I promise if there were some smoke & mirrors drama going on, we'd make it about something more interesting than selling Mullvad add-ons.

comments.author: participant41
comments.body:
> When you buy Tailscale without Mullvad, you don't get exit nodes

Well, you get the ability to run them. And so it could be argued your customers with an Australian billing address should have the exit node functionality blocked on their account.

> When you buy the Tailscale Mullvad add-on

Except arguably you're not even selling Mullvad.

You're charging the full price, but only delivering a quarter of the service.

That's not right, whatever might be going on in the background that you are unwilling or unable to talk about.

Right now, if I'm going to spend $5 a month per user, it 110% makes absolute sense to spend it with Mullvad directly, not Tailscale.

Not only because you are not delivering the full product, but buying it through Tailscale would, from a purely practical perspective, delivering a worse user experience.

If I am in e.g. Japan. On a Tailscale Mullvad subscription.  Where's my nearest exit node on your cut-back list ?   Singapore.

That's what, probaly 70–80ms latency ? Just to get from your device to the exit node.

Meanwhile, Mullvad direct, I get an in-country exit node.

You're welcome to use Mullvad directly if that works for you. The Tailscale integration is for people who don't want to worry about having two VPNs fighting for the same limited system networking hooks. (On many operating systems, different VPNs/networking tools can't coexist well.) > If I am in e.g. Japan. On a Tailscale Mullvad subscription. Where's my nearest exit node on your cut-back list ? Singapore. What is this "cut-back list" you're talking about? If you can buy the Tailscale Mullvad Add-on, you get access to all the Tailscale exit nodes. There's no cut-back list. I see Japan in the list from the Tailscale client: This issue is about countries were we let you buy the Mullvad add-on, not which Mullvad servers that are available.

I told you. If you provide the actual full Mullvad then the integration is great.

But otherwise you are delivering, as I already explained, a poor customer experience.  Because:

1.  people get higher latency on Tailscale Mullvad  than they do under Mullvad direct (e.g. 80ms to an exit node from Japan via Tailscale vs in-country Japan on Mullvad Direct) AND

Those are indisputable facts.

> What is this "cut-back list" you're talking about? 

You know exactly what I am talking about.

I am talking about : https://tailscale.com/kb/1258/mullvad-exit-nodes#available-regions

That list does not match the Mullvad list.

Therefore you are charging full price for a fractional service.   The same $5 spent with Mullvad Direct gets me more, that is a fact.

That is poor.
